359199.title: Alweiss's non-partition-regularity conjecture for sums and products over polynomial colorings
359199.literal_statement:
For $d\in\mathbb{N}$, let $P_d$ be the set of polynomials in a countable set of variables $x_1,x_2,\ldots$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, constant term, and degree at most $d$ in each variable. A pattern is **partition regular over $P_d$** if every finite coloring of $P_d$ contains a monochromatic realization of that pattern.

**Alweiss's non-partition-regularity conjecture.** There exists $n$ such that, for every $d\in\mathbb{N}$, the pattern

$$
\left\{\sum_{i\in S}x_i,\ \prod_{i\in S}x_i: \varnothing\ne S\subseteq[n]\right\}
$$

is not partition regular over $P_d$.

The statement is presented as essentially asserting that the methods of the paper are necessary for addressing Hindman's conjecture over polynomial colorings. It remains open; even the weaker assertion that Hindman's conjecture is false over $P_d$ is not known.

359203.title: SETH-based lower-bound conjecture for Induced Matching on graphs of bounded pathwidth
359203.literal_statement: Let $(G,\ell)$ be an instance of \textsc{Induced Matching}, together with a path decomposition of $G$ of width $\operatorname{pw}$. The Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis (SETH) asserts that, for every $\epsilon>0$, no algorithm solves all such instances in time $(3-\epsilon)^{\operatorname{pw}}\cdot n^{\mathcal{O}(1)}$. **SETH-based lower-bound conjecture.** Unless the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis is false, there does not exist a constant $\epsilon>0$ and an algorithm that, given an instance $(G,\ell)$ together with a path decomposition of $G$ of width $\operatorname{pw}$, solves \textsc{Induced Matching} in $(3-\epsilon)^{\operatorname{pw}}\cdot n^{\mathcal{O}(1)}$ time. This conjectured lower bound would establish that the base $3$ in parameterized algorithms for \textsc{Induced Matching} under pathwidth cannot be improved, assuming SETH.

359276.title: Linear-factor conjecture for semi-external chambers of vector partition functions
359276.literal_statement:
Let $A$ be a $d \times n$ integer matrix of rank $d$, let $f$ be a facet of $\operatorname{pos}_{\mathbb{R}}(A)$ with inner facet normal $\bm{\iota}$, and let $\gamma$ be a semi-external chamber of $A$ intersecting $f$ $(d-1)$-dimensionally. Assume that $\bm{\iota} \cdot \mathbf{c}=1$ for every column $\mathbf{c}$ of $A$ not on $f$, and that the chamber polynomial $p_A^{\gamma}(\mathbf{y})$ is a polynomial. Let $k$ be the number of columns of $A$ not on $f$. **Linear-factor conjecture.** For every chamber of $A$ intersecting $f$ $(d-1)$-dimensionally, the corresponding polynomial $p_A^{\gamma}(\mathbf{y})$ has the linear factors

$$
(\bm{\iota} \cdot \mathbf{y})+i
$$

for $i=1,\dots,k-1$. The conjecture proposes a generalization of the unimodular linear-factor theorem to suitable non-unimodular matrices, where the dot-product condition controls the factors.

359643.title: Kajitani–Miyano–Ueno conjecture on cyclically orderable matroids
359643.literal_statement:
Let $M$ be a matroid with ground set $E(M)$ and rank function $r$. A matroid is **cyclically orderable** if it has a cyclic permutation of its elements such that any $r(M)$ consecutive elements form a basis. For every nonempty subset $X\subseteq E(M)$, define

$$
\beta(X)=\frac{|X|}{r(X)}
$$

when $r(X)\ne 0$, and define $\beta(X)=\infty$ otherwise. Let

$$
\gamma(M)=\max_{\mathchar"001F\ne X\subseteq E(M)}\beta(X).
$$

**Kajitani–Miyano–Ueno conjecture.** The matroid $M$ is cyclically orderable if and only if

$$
\gamma(M)=\beta(E(M)).
$$

Equivalently, this asserts that cyclic orderability is characterized by $|X|/r(X)\le |E(M)|/r(M)$ for every nonempty $X\subseteq E(M)$, with the stated convention when $r(X)=0$. The paper verifies the conjecture for all paving matroids, but the general case is not resolved here.

360388.title: Uniform finite-size criterion for percolation on non-one-dimensional transitive graphs
360388.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal G_d^*$ be the class of infinite transitive graphs of degree $d$ that are not one-dimensional. For a graph $G$ with origin $o$, let $S_r$ be the sphere of radius $r$ around $o$, and write $\mathbb P_p^G(o\leftrightarrow S_r)$ for the probability that $o$ is connected to $S_r$ by an open path. **Uniform finite-size criterion.** For each $d\in\mathbb N$ and $\varepsilon,\delta>0$, there exists $r\in\mathbb N$ such that, for every $G\in\mathcal G_d^*$ and $p\in[0,1]$,

$$
\mathbb P_p^G(o\leftrightarrow S_r)\geq\delta\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathbb P_{p+\varepsilon}^G(o\leftrightarrow\infty)>0.
$$

This is presented as a reformulation of the locality conjecture and is tied to the conjectured continuity of the percolation phase transition. The source says the corresponding continuity question remains open, for example on the three-dimensional cubic lattice.

360806.title: Polymatroid monotonicity conjecture for matroid h*-vectors
360806.literal_statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set, let $\mathrm{P}_1$ and $\mathrm{P}_2$ be polymatroids on $E$, and let $B(\mathrm{P}_1)$ and $B(\mathrm{P}_2)$ denote their base polytopes. Suppose that

$$
B(\mathrm{P}_1)\subseteq B(\mathrm{P}_2).
$$

For a loopless matroid $\mathrm{M}$ on $E$, let $h^*_i(\mathrm{M},\underline{\mathcal{L}}_{B(\mathrm{P})})$ be the $i$th coefficient of the $h^*$-vector associated with the line bundle $\underline{\mathcal{L}}_{B(\mathrm{P})}$. **Polymatroid monotonicity conjecture.** For every loopless matroid $\mathrm{M}$ and every $i$,

$$
h^*_i(\mathrm{M},\underline{\mathcal{L}}_{B(\mathrm{P}_1)})\leq h^*_i(\mathrm{M},\underline{\mathcal{L}}_{B(\mathrm{P}_2)}).
$$

This is inspired by Stanley's monotonicity result for $h^*$-vectors of polytopes and specializes to the corresponding conjecture for the Boolean matroid. Its validity for general loopless matroids remains open.

372758.title: Weak Loewner spectral dominance of the connection matrix over the Dirac matrix
372758.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite abstract simplicial complex with $n$ sets. Let $L$ be the connection matrix and $D$ the Dirac matrix. For a self-adjoint matrix $A$ with eigenvalues $\lambda_1(A)\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_n(A)$, define the spectral sums

$$
S_k(A)=\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j(A).
$$

**Weak Loewner spectral-dominance conjecture.** The matrices $L$ and $D$ satisfy

$$
S_k(L)\geq S_k(D)
$$

for every $1\leq k\leq n$.
The weak Loewner order compares self-adjoint matrices through their ordered spectral sums and is weaker than the usual Loewner order. The paper reports experimental evidence for this inequality but states that it has not yet been proved.

375978.title: Torsion-free groups small-doubling abelianity conjecture
375978.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a torsion-free group and let $S$ be a finite subset of $G$ satisfying

$$
|S|\geq 3,
$$

and $e\in S$, where $e$ is the identity element of $G$. Write $S^2=\{s_1s_2:s_1,s_2\in S\}$ and let $\langle S\rangle$ denote the subgroup generated by $S$.

**Small-doubling abelianity conjecture.** If

$$
|S^2|\leq 3|S|-3,
$$

then $\langle S\rangle$ is an abelian subgroup of $G$.

The source describes this as a further conjecture believed to be true. It would give a general abelianity criterion for sufficiently small product sets in torsion-free groups, beyond the special decompositions into disjoint abelian sets.

368748.title: Ward's divisibility conjecture for Griesmer codes
368748.literal_statement:
Let $C$ be a $[g_q(k,d),k,d]_q$ Griesmer code, where $q=p^f$.

**Ward's divisibility conjecture.** Suppose that $p^e\mid d$ and $p^e\geq q$. Then $p^{e+1}/q$ is a divisor of $C$.

This conjecture seeks to extend Ward's divisibility results for Griesmer codes over nonprime fields. It is motivated by the fact that divisibility over prime fields is stronger, while examples such as the hexacode show that $q^e$-divisibility need not hold when $q=p^f$ with $f>1$; its resolution is not specified here.

368847.title: Alternating Eulerian–Catalan identity for odd n
368847.literal_statement:
Let $n$ be odd. Write $
vDash[n]$ for compositions of $[n]$, let $phi$ range over odd compositions, let $mu_{ell(phi)+1}$ denote the relevant Catalan-number coefficient, and let $E(n,k)$ be the number of permutations of $n$ with $k$ descents.

**Alternating Eulerian–Catalan identity.**

$$
\sum_{\phi\vDash[n] \atop \phi\text{ is odd}}2^{n-\ell(\phi)}\mu_{\ell(\phi)+1}=\sum_{0\leq k\leq n-1}(-1)^kE(n,k).
$$

This identity is reported as an unproved relation between Catalan numbers and Eulerian numbers and is described as irrelevant to the main result of the section.

357167.title: The pinnacle-set enumeration conjecture for signed permutations
357167.literal_statement:
Let $T(n,k)$ be the sequence defined by

$$
T(n,0)=T(n,n)=1
$$

and, for $0<k<n$,

$$
T(n,k)=2T(n-1,k-1)+T(n-1,k).
$$

For each positive integer $n$, let $\mathsf{APS}^B_n$ denote the set of admissible pinnacle sets for signed permutations of size $n$. **Pinnacle-set enumeration conjecture.**

$$
\left|\mathsf{APS}^B_n\right|=T\left(n,\left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor\right).
$$

This conjecture proposes a direct correspondence between the number of admissible pinnacle sets in the hyperoctahedral group and the indicated entries of OEIS sequence A119258. The paper presents it as a possible connection and does not establish the identity in general.

359028.title: Determinant evaluation conjecture for the matrix T_{n,m}(x)
359028.literal_statement:
Let $T_{n,m}(x)$ be the $n\times n$ matrix

$$
T_{n,m}(x):=\left[\binom{x+m}{j-i+m}-\binom{x+m}{m-i-j-1}\right]_{i,j=0}^{n-1}.

**Determinant evaluation conjecture.** The determinant satisfies

$$
\det T_{n,m}(x)=\prod_{i=1}^n\prod_{j=1}^m\frac{(x+i-j)(x+2i+j-2)}{(x+2i-j)(i+j-1)}.
$$

374767.title: Subtree-separation conjecture for the $(n-2,2)$-spectrum of trees
374767.literal_statement:
Let $T$ be a tree on $n$ vertices, and let $M_r^{(2)}(T)$ be its $(n-2,2)$ moments. These moments yield universal support-forest-counting combinations, and the Laplacian spectrum supplies the ordinary vertex-level spectral data. An embedded forest count means the number of copies of the corresponding forest occurring in $T$.

**Subtree separation conjecture.** The universal support-forest-counting combinations arising from $M_r^{(2)}(T)$, together with the Laplacian spectrum, determine all embedded forest counts of $T$. In particular they distinguish trees.

This is presented as a stronger, potentially more approachable form of the spectral support-forest-profile conjecture. It would imply that the combined spectral data reconstruct every embedded forest statistic and hence separate non-isomorphic trees.

363661.title: A common annihilator for resistance numerator and denominator families
363661.literal_statement:
Let a family of graphs have Laplacian matrices, and apply the procedures LaplaceExpand and SystemReduce together with the mathematical theorems described in the source. For banded underlying Laplacians, the same annihilator can be obtained from Laplace expansions of the numerator sequence and also annihilates the denominator; for non-banded Laplacians, the source notes that SystemReduce may need to be applied separately. 372608.title: The Small Quasi-Kernel Conjecture
372608.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a sourceless digraph on $n$ vertices. A **quasi-kernel** is an independent set $Q$ such that every vertex $u$ of $D$ has a vertex $v\in Q$ with $\operatorname{dist}(v,u)\leq 2$.

**Small Quasi-Kernel Conjecture.** The digraph $D$ contains a quasi-kernel of order at most $\frac{n}{2}$.

Sources without vertices have no immediate obstruction from isolated source vertices to a small quasi-kernel, motivating this conjecture of Erdős and Székely from 1976. The conjecture was initially communicated orally and later appeared in print; its status is not resolved in the supplied text.

373504.title: Conjectural overpartition congruence modulo 19
373504.literal_statement:
For a positive integer $n$, let $\overline{p}(n)$ denote the number of overpartitions of $n$, and let $\left(\frac{n}{p}\right)$ denote the Legendre symbol for an odd prime $p$. **Congruence modulo 19.**

$$
\overline{p}(17^2\cdot 4n)\equiv 0\pmod{19},
$$

where $n\equiv 3\pmod 8$, $\left(\frac{n}{17}\right)=-1$, and $\left(\frac{n}{19}\right)=1$. It involves $72$ residue classes modulo $2584$, which the source does not list. The source presents this as another conjectural Ramanujan-type congruence that cannot be proved by the methods in the paper; no resolution is supplied.
